who: Russian saying · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: Repetition is the mother of learning.
meaning: We learn by doing the same thing again and again.

who: Dong Yu, scholar, 3rd century · tr. from Chinese
quote: Someone came to study with Dong Yu. He would not teach him, but said: 'First you must read it a hundred times.' He said: 'Read a book a hundred times, and the meaning shows itself.'
meaning: Don't understand it yet? Do it a hundred times. Then it becomes clear.

quote: By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart.
meaning: We all start out much the same. What we practise again and again makes us different.

who: Svatmarama · Hatha Yoga Pradipika 1.67-68, tr. Pancham Sinh, 1915
quote: Success comes to him who is engaged in the practice. How can one get success without practice; for by merely reading books on Yoga, one can never get success... Practice alone is the means to success.
meaning: Reading about yoga is not enough. Only doing it, again and again, brings success.

quote: There are the footpaths along the hills; if suddenly they be used, they become roads; and if, as suddenly they are not used, the wild grass fills them up.
meaning: Keep walking a path and it becomes a road. Stop, and wild grass covers it again.

who: Vrind · Hindi couplet, 1704, tr. from Hindi
quote: By practising and practising, the dull mind becomes skilled; from the rope coming and going, a mark forms on the stone.
meaning: Keep practising and even a slow learner gets good, like a rope wearing a mark into stone.

who: Epictetus · Discourses II.18, tr. George Long, 1877
quote: ...the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running. ... Generally then if you would make any thing a habit, do it...
meaning: You get good at walking by walking. Want something to become a habit? Do it.

who: William James · The Principles of Psychology, 1890
quote: Never suffer an exception to occur till the new habit is securely rooted in your life. Each lapse is like the letting fall of a ball of string which one is carefully winding up...
meaning: While a new habit is young, do not skip a day. One slip undoes many days of work.

quote: Grind an anvil down into a needle.
meaning: Keep at it, with all your heart, until it works.
Use your legs every day, and you keep strong legs.
